thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high severity - logging-forwarder S3 -> external-analytics bucket spike (10x). Sampled header snippets found containing 'session=' tokens in uploaded objects. Automated detector flagged possible PII leak.

jordan: acknowledged. I'm oncall. setting priority P0.

priya: copying logs now. can we block the forwarder egress to that bucket immediately?

jordan: yes. priya, can you add a temporary deny on the forwarder role to that specific bucket and rotate the forwarder service key?

priya: on it. running policy patch. will also create a read-only snapshot of the last 24h uploads to preserve evidence.

kai: product note - we think this is the sampling feature in the logging-agent (enabled for analytics). might have pulled header fragments by config mistake. customer impact unknown yet.

mike-legal: please preserve all artifacts. do NOT delete any objects. legal hold requested until we assess scope. also capture requester IPs and bucket ACL changes.

jordan: got it. priya, don't delete. we need a pointer to the earliest suspect object.

priya: found objects with key prefix logs/forwarder/2024-03-01/ -> sample objects contain header lines like: 
```
session=eyJhbGci... partial-token
user-agent: curl/7.68.0
```
I'll copy the object metadata to a secure evidence bucket (privileged access only).

priya: policy applied: iam:DetachRolePolicy to forwarder-role -> DENY s3:PutObject to arn:aws:s3:::external-analytics-bucket/* . service key rotate queued.

jordan: nice. can you post the command output?

priya: `aws iam put-role-policy --role-name logging-forwarder --policy-name block-external-put --policy-document file://deny.json` -> status OK.

sally: paging: reached out to affected customer success lead to prep potential notice. no known customer complaints yet.

kai: quick impact check: are these real session tokens or vanity sampling IDs? initial grep shows base64-like strings and some UUIDs.

priya: sample contents (sanitized) -> `session=***REDACTED***; path=/; HttpOnly` looks like session cookie fragments, not full JWTs in all cases.

mike-legal: still treat as high risk. keep chain of custody notes (who touched what and when). document commands.

jordan: action plan: 1) contain (priya) block egress + rotate forwarder key; 2) preserve evidence (priya + sally) copy objects to evidence-bucket; 3) assess scope (jordan + kai) run grep across last 7 days; 4) customer comms (sally + cs); 5) legal hold (mike-legal). I'll own coordination.

priya: rotate started: `aws iam create-access-key --user forwarder-service` -> new key created, old key deactivated. propagation in 60s.

jordan: verify no further uploads after deny timestamp.

priya: upload rate dropped to baseline. last PutObject at 1709805605.

jordan: approved. good. kai, please run the scope grep and give counts by environment (prod/staging).

kai: running: `s3cmd ls s3://external-analytics-bucket/logs/ | xargs -n1 -I{} s3cmd get s3://external-analytics-bucket/{}` then grep for "session=" -> results: prod: 42 objects with matches, staging: 7. earliest match 1709720000.

jordan: 42 prod objects. sally, start drafting a short customer impact checklist: potential exposure, what we rotated, mitigation steps, ETA for deeper forensics.

sally: drafting now. will include rotated keys, blocked forwarder, evidence preserved, timeline, and remediation recommendations.

mike-legal: recommend no customer notice until we confirm whether full session tokens can be reconstructed and whether any customer PII was included. but prepare a pre-written notice.

jordan: agreed. forops - please capture network flow logs for any external IPs that pulled these objects and list unique requesters. priya can you get requestor IPs from object metadata?

priya: yes - listing metadata now. unique requester IPs: [203.0.113.12, 198.51.100.45] (both belong to analytics vendor ASN).

jordan: ok. escalation: contact vendor security and ask for retention / deletion of objects. sally, can you open a formal channel with their SOC?

sally: opening contact now. sending them object keys and legal hold note. :envelope_with_arrow:

kai: for internal followup: disable sampling header field in logging-agent config across clusters and push a config rollback.

priya: pushed config patch to disable header sampling in k8s DaemonSet. `kubectl rollout restart ds/logging-agent` -> rollout started.

jordan: good. checklist status?

priya: contain: done. rotate: in-progress (old key deactivated). preserve: done (copies in evidence-bucket). config rollback: in-progress.

kai: scope: initial count done (42 prod). deeper content evaluation ongoing.

mike-legal: preserve chain-of-custody logs in case regulators ask. keep timeline in Confluence under incident-1709805551.

jordan: will keep this channel for live updates. if anyone sees further spikes re-ping. thanks all. :thumbsup:
